sovereign_country.strategic_role: 连接拉美市场的欧洲商贸桥梁、本地化仓配与数字游民签证

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (state-wide unitary jurisdiction; no separate sub-state tax registry for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental European; corporate law codified in Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital; regional foral civil law specialties do not alter SL incorporation rules)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain–Mexico Reciprocal Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (APPRI, 2006)
Spain–Chile Reciprocal Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (APPRI, 1993)
Spain–Colombia Reciprocal Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (APPRI, 2007)
Spain–Peru Reciprocal Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (APPRI, 1998)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (arts. 3, 4, 13, 31–32); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (Reglamento); Real Decreto 346/2023, de 9 de mayo (Registro de Titularidades Reales); Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, arts. 203–204)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Vigencia) of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company/commercial registry of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if originating in a Hague Convention state) OR Consular Legalization (if originating in a non-Hague state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Estatutos Sociales) of the corporate shareholder, including amendments currently in force
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder's registry or notary of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Register Certificate or shareholder ledger evidencing the ultimate beneficial ownership chain up to the 25% statutory threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent UBO register or corporate secretary of the shareholder's origin jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial Power of Attorney (Poder Notarial) appointing the Spanish incorporation attorney or legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, proposed directors/administrators, signatories and UBOs against (i) United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) EU consolidated financial sanctions, including Council Regulation (EC) 2580/2001 and (EC) 881/2002; (iii) Spanish domestic sanctions, judicial/administrative enforcement alerts and SEPBLAC warnings; and (iv) PEP databases for domestic and foreign public officials under Ley 10/2010 arts. 3–4 and FATF standards. OFAC SDN screening is included as prudent market standard because USD-based SaaS payment rails (Paddle and Lemon Squeezy) will be used. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory where a PEP is identified, the UBO chain is opaque, or funds originate in a FATF high-risk third country listed in Real Decreto 304/2014.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) – Certification of Negative Company Name (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social); online submission via the Sede Electrónica del Registro Mercantil Central / Ministry of Justice e-services (at rmc.es).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil), arts. 178–181, the company name must be written in Latin alphabet, in Spanish or any other language, but for registry search and identity comparison it is transliterated and normalized to Spanish phonetics; accents, hyphens and spaces do not avoid similarity. The registered name must include the legal-type designator 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or 'S.L.' immediately after the chosen name, and it must not be contrary to law, morality, public order or apt to create ambiguity with public administrations, notional bodies, existing companies or registered trademarks.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Gobierno / Administración / Ministerio / Consejo de Estado (prior ministerial authorization required)
Banco de España (prior ministerial authorization required)
S.A. / S.L.U. / S. Com. por A. / S. Cooperativa / Fundación / Mutua (reserved to other legal forms; prohibited in an SL name)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, of 2 July), arts. 19-23, 36-38, 208-219, 251-252; Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Real Decreto 1784/1996); Ley 18/2022 de creación y crecimiento de empresas (Crea y Crece), arts. 15-16.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Mercantile Registry) and the Provincial Mercantile Registry of the province where the registered office is established.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (deed of incorporation executed before a Spanish public notary and subsequently filed for registration in the Mercantile Registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard SL requires EUR 3,000 of share capital fully subscribed and paid into a blocked Spanish escrow bank account; under the 'Sociedad de Formación Sucesiva' regime (art. 4.4 LSC), incorporation with a capital below EUR 3,000 (minimum EUR 1) is permitted, subject to legal reserve and distribution restrictions until the EUR 3,000 threshold is reached.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — By unanimous written resolution of the sole incorporator acting as founder shareholder, at the inaugural general meeting held on [date], it is resolved: (1) To accept the subscription of the totality of the corporate share capital by the founder, and to acknowledge full payment of the minimum statutory capital into a blocked escrow account; (2) To adopt as the registered office of the company the Spanish address designated for legal notifications, authorizing the commencement of business; (3) To appoint [Name] as sole administrator and legal representative, and [Name] as non-assistant secretary, granting the administrator the broadest powers under law, including the power to execute, sign, and file all incorporation filings with the Mercantile Registry and tax authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Spanish tax identification numbers for founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) / Provincial Tax Office (Delegación de Hacienda)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For non-resident individuals, apply for a NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) at the local immigration office or Spanish consulate, and for a provisional tax identification number (NIF) if not yet resident. Resident founders should apply directly through the AEAT portal or in person. Submit the completed application, passport, and proof of economic interest in Spain. The NIE is a prerequisite for any notarized incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Completed EX-15 or EX-01 application form
Original and copy of passport or EU ID
Proof of appointment or application fee payment
Supporting evidence of incorporation purpose (e.g., draft deed or business plan)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, rectify missing documentation, re-submit through the same window or digitally, and request a formal written resolution; appeal within one month to the relevant administrative body if refused.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public incorporation deed before a Spanish notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (Notaría) of the jurisdiction where the registered office is established
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the corporate name certificate (obtained from the Central Mercantile Registry), the founders' NIE/TIE, the draft bylaws (estatutos), and proof of capital deposit in a blocked escrow bank account. The notary will read the deed, verify identity and capacity of the incorporators, and execute the Escritura de Constitución. The notary issues the first copy for registration and the deed tax (AJJD) declaration.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación) issued by the Central Mercantile Registry
Draft Escritura de Constitución and estatutos
Proof of deposit of paid-up capital (blocked bank certificate)
Identity and NIE/TIE details of all incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects, correct the drafting or documentation and resubmit for a new appointment; a defective deed can be re-executed within 30 days without additional registry fees if the same transaction is corrected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay the Documented Legal Acts Tax (AJJD) and obtain the provisional NIF/CIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) / Provincial Tax Office (Oficina Liquidadora)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the executed deed to the regional tax office within thirty working days to file form Modelo 600 for the Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados. The tax rate for incorporation of SLs ranges from 0.5% to 1.5% depending on the autonomous community. Simultaneously, apply for the provisional CIF (tax identification number for companies) using the AEAT form 030, which will be issued immediately upon presentation of the deed and tax payment receipt.
required_dossiers: Executed public deed (first copy or certified copy)
Modelo 600 form (regional tax liquidation)
Modelo 030 form (for provisional CIF)
Proof of payment of the AJJD tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office rejects the deed or requests additional information, provide a certified translation or supplementary deed within the statutory window; late filing penalties can be reduced by submitting a solicitud de aplazamiento or correcting the self-assessment before formal inspection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of deed execution, submit the first copy of the deed and the executed Modelo 600 tax payment form to the Mercantile Registry corresponding to the registered office province. The registrar reviews the legality of the deed and bylaws, and, if approved, the registration is entered and public notice is published in the Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME). Registration is constitutive for the company's full legal capacity.
required_dossiers: First copy or certified copy of the Escritura de Constitución
Modelo 600 receipt or proof of tax payment
Certificate of the negative name (if requested by the registrar)
Payment of registry fee (tarifa del Registro Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registrars have three terms of approximately ten working days to return a deficiency note (calificación adversa). On receipt, submit corrected documents or an alleged appeal (recurso gubernativo) to the General Directorate or registry authority within one month, or pay the purchase fee and finalize registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain definitive CIF, register with Social Security, and apply for municipal operating clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS); local Ayuntamiento (municipal authority)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration in the Mercantile Registry, file form 030 again to obtain the definitive CIF (NIF) permanently within one month. If the company will have employees, register as an employer with the Seguridad Social and obtain a constituent code (código de cuenta de cotización) via TOT-Social system. For a micro-SaaS with no physical premises, no municipal activity license (licencia de actividad) is required, but a mere prior activity notification (declaración responsable) may be filed if a home office is used; for commercial premises, obtain the municipal occupancy/running license or exemption.
required_dossiers: Registry registration certificate (certificación de inscripción)
Modelo 030 definitive CIF application
Employer registration form TA.6 (if hiring staff)
Municipal declaration of responsible party or license application (if physical location)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive CIF is delayed, submit a written reminder to the AEAT and request the provisional NIF to continue operations; if the municipality queries the declaration responsible, provide proof of the software-service activity and update the declaration to comply with zoning restrictions; administrative silence after 30 days (for declarations) is positive approval.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the micro-SaaS activity (ISIC 6201, NAICS 511210) is a non-industrial cloud software service; no industrial establishment license is required under Spanish law.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — a mere prior activity declaration (declaración responsable) may be required if physical business premises are used, but no operational or manufacturing permit applies to the digital subscription service.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable — no physical facility or manufacturing process triggers environmental assessment; if an office lease is signed, the landlord’s energy and environmental compliance suffices under RD 486/1997 and RD 664/2011.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — micro-SaaS software development and cloud operations are excluded from the annexes of Law 21/2013 (Environmental Assessment); no EIA or environmental permit required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — data-center operations are handled by third-party cloud providers (e.g., Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) under their environmental compliance; the company itself has no wastewater, VOC, or waste disposal activities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for a virtual micro-SaaS entity with no physical operational site. If the company later occupies business premises or hires staff, the employer must perform a workplace risk assessment under the Ley de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales (Law 31/1995) and obtain a fire safety conformity sign-off (certificado de protección contra incendios) from the local fire service; otherwise no fire-safety certification is required at formation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Spanish Tax Agency, official portal at https://www.aeat.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish entities including SL obtain NIF automatically upon incorporation and registration with the Mercantile Registry. Non-resident entities must apply for NIF through the AEAT online portal using an official form accompanied by apostilled supporting documents or via a duly authorized tax representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available under Spanish law. Corporate income tax is levied at the entity level. Limited hybrid mismatch adjustments permitted under EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory issuance of electronic invoices in Facturae format for B2B transactions; real-time reporting obligation via AEAT's SII (Immediate Supply Information) system with digital stamping and QR code verification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods to third countries outside the EU and to certain cross-border services provided to non-EU customers, requiring verifiable proof of export or service performance outside Spain.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Administrative penalties ranging from 100% to 200% of the evaded VAT amount, plus statutory interest and potential criminal liability for intentional false declarations or fraudulent claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, acting under the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise and the applicable European Union framework, including the European Central Bank, the European Central Bank foreign exchange regime, the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, the Spanish Law 19/2003 on the Legal Regime of Capital Movements and Economic Transactions Abroad, and Royal Decree 1816/1991 as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies broad freedom of capital movements and current-account convertibility within the European Union. The euro is freely convertible for ordinary commercial payments, service receipts, dividends, interest, royalties, loan repayments, capital contributions, and other lawful cross-border transactions. Spain does not generally impose prior foreign-exchange approval, mandatory conversion into euros, exchange surrender, or restrictions on the repatriation of lawful profits. Practical hurdles are principally bank-level anti-money-laundering, sanctions, beneficial-owner, source-of-funds, transfer-pricing, tax-residency, and transaction-purpose controls. Dividend or other profit remittances require distributable accounting profits, compliance with Spanish corporate-law reserve rules, approval of the relevant corporate resolution, withholding-tax analysis, and supporting accounting records. Payments to non-residents may require Spanish withholding unless an applicable treaty or European Union exemption is properly documented. Foreign direct investment reporting, statistical reporting to Banco de España, and transaction-specific sanctions or national-security controls may apply without constituting general currency-convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement for an exporter to surrender export proceeds to a Spanish bank, convert a prescribed percentage into euros, or repatriate receipts within a fixed period. Export proceeds may generally remain in euro or foreign-currency accounts, subject to ordinary banking, tax, accounting, sanctions, and anti-money-laundering controls. The company must retain commercial invoices, contracts, shipping or service evidence, customer identification, and payment records sufficient to substantiate the transaction. Banco de España statistical reporting may apply to external assets and liabilities or cross-border transactions, depending on the reporting instrument and applicable thresholds; the reporting frequency and threshold are determined by the relevant Banco de España reporting framework and may change. Cash or bearer negotiable instruments transported into or out of the European Union with a value of EUR 10,000 or more require the applicable customs declaration. No mandatory conversion ratio or statutory export-receipt conversion deadline applies to a Spanish SL conducting ordinary software exports.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Capital Contribution Account where the bank accepts transaction-specific capital documentation. A separate statutory capital escrow account is not generally required for an SL, particularly because Spanish law permits formation with capital below the former EUR 3,000 threshold subject to statutory protections.
Operational Account; Capital Contribution Account where supported by the incorporation and notarial documentation.
Operational Account; Capital Contribution Account for incorporation or subsequent equity funding, subject to source-of-funds and corporate-document review.
Operational Account; Capital Contribution Account where accepted under the bank's corporate onboarding policy.
Operational Account; Capital Contribution Account subject to Spanish corporate registration, beneficial-owner verification, and funding evidence.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment collection and operating flows, but not a complete substitute for a Spanish commercial bank. A European Economic Area electronic money institution or payment institution may provide EUR payment accounts, SEPA transfers, cards, safeguarding, and certain foreign-currency services under its home-state authorization and passporting framework. Paddle and Lemon Squeezy should be treated as merchant-of-record or payment-collection providers, not as unrestricted corporate banking substitutes. The SL must verify merchant-of-record terms, settlement ownership, chargeback allocation, tax invoicing, VAT evidence, reserve rights, restricted-business rules, sanctions screening, and payout-country eligibility. Offshore or non-EEA digital EMIs may require local licensing or reliance on a licensed EEA partner for services provided to Spanish customers. EMI safeguarding does not equal deposit insurance, and account closure, reserve, transaction-limit, and enhanced-review risks are material. Maintain at least one regulated Spanish or EEA bank account for tax payments, payroll, statutory obligations, and business continuity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be available through qualified electronic identification, video identification, electronic signature, or bank-specific procedures. In practice, banks may require a director, authorized signatory, beneficial owner, or controlling person to attend physically or complete a live video interview, particularly where ownership is non-resident, the business is newly incorporated, documents are foreign-issued, the operating model is digital-only, or the expected flows are international. A notarial power of attorney may permit an agent to act for selected steps, but it does not necessarily eliminate beneficial-owner or management interviews. The company should prepare Spanish or sworn translations where requested and preserve originals and apostilles or legalizations for foreign documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, beneficial owner, or authorized signatory with incomplete identity, tax-residence, or address evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport or national identity document; current proof of residential address; Spanish NIE where applicable; tax-residence certificate; ownership chart to the ultimate natural persons; beneficial-owner declaration; corporate registry extracts; notarized powers of attorney; apostille or legalization and certified translation where required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SL with no operating history, no local employees, or no Spanish commercial premises.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deed of incorporation; current Registro Mercantil certificate; NIF; articles of association; director appointment evidence; business plan; product description; website and terms of service; customer acquisition model; supplier and contractor agreements; projected monthly volumes; tax registrations; explanation of remote-work and outsourcing arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Micro-SaaS model using Paddle, Lemon Squeezy, or other merchant-of-record platforms, creating payment flows inconsistent with the company's direct customer profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant-of-record agreement; platform onboarding approval; settlement statements; payment-flow diagram; customer geography; refund and chargeback policy; subscription terms; VAT and invoicing treatment; evidence that the company provides lawful software services and does not process prohibited goods, financial products, or regulated activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained inbound capital from an offshore shareholder, group company, founder, or third-party account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital-increase or shareholder-loan agreement; board and shareholder resolutions; subscription documentation; bank statements evidencing source of funds; audited or management accounts of the funder; beneficial-owner information; tax-residence documents; transfer-pricing analysis for related-party debt; payment instruction identifying the legal purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume or high-frequency foreign-currency receipts and payments relative to the stated micro-SaaS activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling 12-month cash-flow forecast; transaction-volume reconciliation; customer and supplier concentration analysis; invoices and contracts; platform reports; foreign-exchange policy; expected currencies and countries; explanation of refunds, subscription renewals, intercompany flows, and treasury controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving higher-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned territories, politically exposed persons, or opaque intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete counterparty identification; beneficial-owner screening; sanctions and PEP screening results; underlying contract and invoice; end-use statement; shipping or service-delivery evidence; legal review of applicable sanctions; written compliance approval; prohibition on indirect routing designed to evade controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between registered business activity, ISIC classification, website claims, and actual payment purposes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated corporate-purpose statement where necessary; software architecture and product documentation; customer contracts; invoices; accounting ledgers; management certification; evidence that the activity is ordinary software operation and does not constitute payment services, lending, crypto-asset services, gambling, employment intermediation, or another regulated activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax, accounting, or corporate-record inconsistencies, including missing annual accounts, inactive tax status, or unexplained related-party payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax identification evidence; filed tax returns; accounting trial balance; annual accounts and filing receipts; shareholder and director registers; intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing support; reconciliation of bank statements to the general ledger; certificate of good standing or equivalent registry evidence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity funding through the SL's account with a Spanish or EEA-regulated bank using SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments or SWIFT cross-border transfer for other currencies. The remittance should identify the legal purpose as share capital, share premium, capital increase, or shareholder loan, as applicable, and name the Spanish SL as beneficiary. Use the company's registered name, NIF, IBAN, BIC, registered address, and a consistent payment reference. Before receipt, provide the bank with the executed subscription or loan agreement, corporate approvals, notarial or registry evidence where available, beneficial-owner information, source-of-funds evidence, and any required foreign-investment declaration information. Do not route capital through personal accounts, unrelated group entities, payment aggregators, or nominee accounts. Reconcile the received amount to the corporate resolution and accounting records. A capital contribution does not become subscribed share capital merely because funds reach the bank account; the applicable Spanish corporate-law formalities, notarial deed, and Commercial Registry filing must be completed where required. Confirm whether the bank, Banco de España, or the competent investment authority requires statistical or foreign-investment reporting for the specific transaction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area, subject to bank limits and fraud controls. Use SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly documented through an MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA or non-euro payments. For recurring software suppliers and contractors, use verified beneficiary master data, dual approval, invoice matching, sanctions screening, and callback verification for bank-account changes. For material or jurisdictionally sensitive purchases, use a documentary commercial letter of credit, standby letter of credit, or bank guarantee where commercially justified; the bank will require applicant credit approval, compliant underlying contracts, documentary conditions, and sanctions screening. A software company should not use a commercial LC merely as a substitute for normal invoice settlement unless the transaction profile supports it. Retain invoices, contracts, delivery or service evidence, VAT analysis, withholding-tax analysis, and payment confirmations. For non-resident service providers, assess Spanish withholding, treaty documentation, permanent-establishment risk, transfer pricing, and deductibility before payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a regulated bank or authorized investment firm, used to hedge identifiable forecast or committed exposures and documented under appropriate treasury confirmations.

Non-deliverable forwards, where offered and legally permitted by the counterparty's licensing regime, generally cash-settled in a reference currency and subject to counterparty eligibility, product governance, sanctions controls, and applicable derivatives reporting.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented liquidity or debt exposures, subject to counterparty credit approval, collateral terms, EMIR obligations, reporting, valuation, and close-out documentation.
FX spot transactions for operational conversion of receipts and payments, with segregation of trading authority, independent confirmation, and transaction records.

Plain-vanilla currency options or collars may be used only after a suitability, appropriateness, cost, accounting, and downside-risk review; complex or leveraged products are inappropriate for routine micro-SaaS treasury unless specifically approved.

Hedging transactions should be executed with EU-authorized credit institutions or investment firms under documented master agreements, such as an ISDA Master Agreement or equivalent bank documentation. Apply EMIR clearing, margin, reporting, risk-mitigation, and trade-repository requirements according to the product, counterparty classification, and applicable thresholds. Maintain a board-approved policy defining permitted instruments, hedge ratios, tenor limits, counterparty limits, collateral, accounting treatment, and prohibition of speculative trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales): audited or unaudited financial statements, application of results, and management report approved by the ordinary shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) corresponding to the registered office; transmitted electronically via the Registro Mercantil Central
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by the ordinary general meeting within six months of the fiscal year end and deposit within one month of approval; for a 31 December year end, deposit is due on or before 30 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The registry refuses to inscribe any further corporate instrument (share transfers, director appointments, capital changes) until the arrears are cured; directorship exposure to coercive fines (multas coercitivas) under Article 283 of the Spanish Capital Companies Act; after two consecutive years of non-deposit, loss of access to public subsidies and public procurement and a permanent 'cuentas no depositadas' annotation on the registry sheet

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Legalization of Corporate Books (Legalización de Libros): journal (Libro Diario), inventories and annual accounts book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales), and, as applicable, register of members and minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) before the registrar or via approved electronic legalization service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months following the fiscal year close, i.e. on or before 30 April for a calendar-year entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late presentation is accepted only with an increased registry tariff; unlegalized books lack formal evidentiary value, weaken the deposit of annual accounts, and expose administrators to penalties for defective accounting records under the Commercial Code and Spanish General Tax Law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Declaration and Re-Confirmation (Declaración de Titularidad Real): identification of natural-person owners and controllers maintained in the Registro Central de Titularidades Reales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Central de Titularidades Reales (RTR), filed through a notary, the Mercantile Registry, or the annual accounts deposit page (Identificación del titular real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial declaration within ten business days of incorporation; updated declaration within thirty calendar days of any direct or indirect transfer of participaciones or change of control; annual re-confirmation delivered simultaneously with the deposit of annual accounts, generally by 30 July for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Sanctionable as an infringement under Spanish anti-money-laundering Law 10/2010 with administrative fines ranging up to EUR 60,000 for minor infringements and EUR 60,001–1,500,000 for serious infringements depending on classification, recidivism and culpability; outstanding UBO filings may additionally block registry operations on the company's corporate file

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard Spanish Corporate Income Tax rate for Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday. Newly created qualifying companies pay 15% on the first EUR 300,000 of annual taxable base for the first tax period and the immediately following tax period, with 25% on the excess. R&D tax credits for software development may further reduce the effective rate; the Micro-SaaS classification alone does not create a preferential CIT rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory expiry; an annual offset limitation applies only to taxpayers with net turnover above EUR 20 million, so not relevant for a Micro-SaaS)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 — Annual CIT return; mandatory electronic filing at AEAT Sede Electrónica using digital certificate, Cl@ve PIN, or registered representative authorisation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the filing window is 1–25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select 'Normal' for the ordinary annual return or 'Complementaria' for a corrective return after a previous filing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ownership by non-residents does not change the filing type; the Spanish SL files as a resident entity under its Spanish NIF.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate the tax period start and end dates. A new SL generally starts on incorporation and closes on the same day 12 months later.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Keep the period aligned with the capital contribution date and the accounting year; non-resident shareholder data is not entered here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial accounting result adjusted for tax reconciliation items, less eligible loss carryforwards. For SaaS, deferred revenue prepayments under Spanish GAAP are reversed for tax purposes when billed unless properly accrued under the applicable recognition rule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign end-user revenue is not automatically foreign-source: a Spanish-resident SL is taxed on worldwide income. The non-resident status of shareholders is irrelevant for this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 – Cuota íntegra y cuota líquida
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 25% statutory rate (or 15% if newly created and qualifying), subtract R&D credits, double taxation relief, withholdings, and quarterly advance payments to produce net tax payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividend withholding obligations to non-resident shareholders are reported in Modelo 123, not in this corporate tax return box.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior AEAT requirement: graduated surcharge of 5% of the tax due if filed within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, 20% after 12 months, plus late payment interest. If the final tax due is zero, a flat EUR 100 penalty may be imposed. Intentional misstatements trigger additional penalties under Articles 191 and 193 LGT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 — Pagos fraccionados (quarterly CIT advance payment); submitted electronically to AEAT.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Advance payments are due on 1–20 April, 1–20 October, and 1–20 December each year for the first, second, and third quarters respectively.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the corporate NIF, name, and the period end date of the preceding tax year used to compute the instalment base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's NIF; a foreign beneficial owner's tax identification is not reflected in this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mark the applicable computation method: 'base' method based on the documented result of the previous year, or the flat-rate method for entities under certain conditions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The method is selected by the Spanish entity regardless of shareholder residence; AEAT may reject inconsistent changes after a pattern of refunds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base multiplied by the applicable rate (25% standard or 15% new-company), reduced by withholdings and prior instalments, yielding the amount payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is a Spanish CIT prepayment; it cannot be reduced because the shareholders are foreign residents, and it is not included in the shareholders' home-country credit until the final annual assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted Modelo 202 payments attract Article 27 LGT surcharges of 5%, 10%, 15%, or 20% on the unpaid instalment plus late interest; total non-declaration may produce a 50% penalty under Article 191 LGT.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% domestic withholding tax on dividends paid by a Spanish SL to non-resident shareholders; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the parent holds at least 5% for one year and meets substance requirements; reduced to 0–15% under applicable double tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must provide the Spanish payor with a valid certificate of tax residence (TRC) and a beneficial ownership declaration before the dividend date to apply the treaty/directive rate at source. If excess withholding has been charged, the shareholder must file Modelo 210 for a refund within four years, together with the TRC and evidence of economic substance when requested under the Principal Purpose Test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents: 24% statutory withholding; interest paid to non-residents: 19% statutory withholding. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive may exempt associated companies (generally 25% direct participation, both EU-resident, no hybrid mismatch) and DTA provisions commonly reduce royalty and interest withholding to 0–10% depending on the reciprocal jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File documentation is triggered when the Spanish entity's net turnover in the preceding tax year exceeds EUR 10,000,000. Master File and Country-by-Country Reporting obligations apply for group/consolidated revenue of EUR 750,000,000 or more. A Micro-SaaS below these thresholds is not automatically exempt from the arm's-length principle; contemporaneous records should still support intercompany pricing if related-party transactions exist.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations certificate regime. Instead, the following apply: (i) the general anti-abuse rule under Article 15 LIS gives priority to economic reality; (ii) tax treaty and EU Directive benefits require genuine business activity, local management, employees or credible operational/infrastructure presence; and (iii) a shell SL used solely to route SaaS revenues or to hoard IP without substance may be disregarded, its income recharacterised, and its directors exposed to personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and false accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting online subscription revenue, issuing sham invoices to overseas payment intermediaries, or artificially deferring SaaS revenue to a controlled foreign entity merely to avoid Spanish CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax penalties of 50% to 150% of the under-declared tax under LGT Articles 191 and 193. Where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax year, criminal liability arises under Criminal Code Article 305, with imprisonment of one to five years and fines up to six times the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly caused or facilitated the non-payment may be jointly and severally liable under Article 43.1 LGT, may be criminally convicted as principals, and may be subject to travel bans, provisional custody, and asset freezes during proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of corporate personality / shell company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming a Spanish SL purely to fabricate an EU legal presence, with nominee directors, no office, no managerial decision-making, no employees, and the entire global SaaS subscription revenue artificially transferred to a non-resident shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Courts and AEAT may 'lift the corporate veil' ('levantamiento del velo'), deny treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test, recharacterise the taxable beneficiary, apply the Article 15 LIS general anti-abuse rule, and issue penalties of 50%-150% of the adjusted tax positions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors face personal civil and fiscal liability, disqualification orders, and criminal exposure to fraud and economic crime charges; international search measures may impose travel bans and judicial controls.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Executing related-party transactions (e.g., management fees, IP licence payments to shareholder, offshore processor commissions) without contemporaneous arm's-length benchmarking, or using a gross margin that obtains no net profit in Spain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may make a transfer pricing adjustment under Article 18 LIS plus interest; failure to produce mandatory documentation can trigger penalties of up to EUR 30,000 or a percentage of the adjusted amount, and systematic non-compliance may lead to hidden-charge assessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the transfer pricing deficiency results in non-payment of a material agreed tax charge, directors can be declared jointly liable under Article 43.1 LGT and prosecuted for tax evasion when the adjusted unpaid tax exceeds the criminal threshold.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting SaaS subscription payments through unregulated crypto or offshore payment rails without beneficial-owner identification, mixing business receipts with personal wallets, failing to report suspicious transactions, or acting as a mule for sanctions-avoidance payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Infringements of Law 10/2010 carry fines of up to EUR 5,000,000 or up to 200% of the value of the transaction; criminal money laundering under Criminal Code Articles 301–304 can result in imprisonment of up to six years and confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the absence of AML controls, may be criminally convicted for laundering proceeds if they were active in the scheme, and can be subjected to travel bans, precautionary detention, and statutory disqualification from managing companies.
